az_tall_wall_the.blurb: A small cliff of five routes beside Boulder Creek in the Granite Dells near Prescott, tucked along the Peavine Trail. The sport and trad lines are spread over two faces and run mostly 5.9 to 5.10, with a single 5.11. The creek carries water for several months of the year, which gives the spot a quiet, scenic feel. The tallest section calls for a 70 m rope to top-rope or rappel, while a 60 m rope covers the left half of one face and every route on the other. Riding a bike in saves time on the walk.
az_tall_wall_the.approach: Walk or ride the Peavine Trail for about a mile and a half until a bike rack stands on the eastern side, go through the gate, then keep beside the creek until the bolted formation comes into view.

az_crossbones_boulder.blurb: A single boulder in the Rappel Rock bouldering zone on Mount Lemmon, high in the Santa Catalina Mountains above Tucson. It holds five problems, starting with an easy V1 warm-up, then a pair of V3s, a V6 and a V8 at the top end. The stone is of excellent quality and the problem that gives the boulder its name is described as unmissable. It hides behind trees a short way off the climbers' trail that leads down to Rappel Rock, so look for it once the trail passes the steep slabs.

az_golder_dome.blurb: A clean dome of roughly 500 feet on the northwest side of the Santa Catalina Mountains, above the town of Catalina north of Tucson. Most lines are four or five pitches with a blend of bolts and natural gear, with a few shorter routes alongside. All five climbs here are trad, spanning 5.8 to 5.12 but clustered around 5.9 and 5.10. A broad gully divides the face: the left half stays sunny until mid-morning, and the right half picks up sun late in the afternoon. Route-finding can be technical, two ropes are usually needed to rappel, and a knife and spare webbing are worth carrying.

az_lv_deadpoint_boulder.blurb: A small boulder in the Linda Vista bouldering zone on the northwest side of the Santa Catalina Mountains outside Tucson. It stands right beside the bigger Art boulder and is among the first blocks reached after leaving the trail. Five problems are listed: one easy V1, two V4s, a V6 and a hard V8, so it mainly rewards climbers already comfortable in the mid grades. The approach from the trailhead is short, and the wider area offers a few days of moderate bouldering and roped climbing.

az_moran_point.blurb: A handful of boulder problems at a South Rim viewpoint in Grand Canyon National Park, found along Desert View Drive more than twelve miles east of Grand Canyon Village. The stone is pale limestone, and the blocks are scattered around the point, with the most concentrated on its east side. Five problems are listed, three of them V0, plus a V1 and a V3, which makes this a gentle outing for newer boulderers. Rim boulders here sit close to the road and come with big canyon views.

az_bedrock.blurb: A short, steep sport wall within The Pit, the pocketed limestone crag just south of Flagstaff along Lake Mary Road. Bedrock sits in an alcove right beside The Shooting Gallery and is covered in pockets. It holds five bolted routes: three in the 5.10 range and two at 5.11, which suits climbers stepping up from moderates. Two of the Pit's best moderate lines are here. The Pit as a whole can be climbed in any season.
